title: POC Onboarding Labsheet — Inference Factory
content:
Purpose:
Quick labsheet to run a lean customer POC for the ‘Inference Factory’ integration. This is intentionally lightweight — goal is to validate latency, cost per inference, and quality parity for the customer’s chat assistant use case within a 3-week sprint. Use this doc for workshop prep, deployment checklist, and acceptance rubric.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: single-model serving (quantized variant supported), cloud-hosted Redwood Dedicated demo, datastore integration for prompt context (S3-like blob store), sample prompt set evaluation, workshop for customer engineers and product.
- Out of scope: full multi-region rollout, on-prem air-gapped installation, custom model training.

Primary stakeholders:
- Customer PM: Anika Rao (customer side)
- Internal SE lead: Samira Chen (owner)
- Infra support: Ethan Morales
- Eval & quality: Priya Natarajan
- Account exec: Diego Alvarez

Success criteria (must pass to consider POC successful) — acceptance split into objective and subjective:
1) Objective metrics (quantitative) — measured on a 48-hour production-like load window:
   - 95th percentile response latency for 512-token responses <= 420 ms when using dedicated pool and batching policy alpha-1.
   - Median cost per 1K tokens <= $0.95 (after suggested batching/quantization).
   - Availability >= 99.5% over test window (no more than ~3 hours of cumulative error time across 48 hours).
   - Throughput: sustain 40 concurrent chat sessions with average qps 12 without queue growth.
2) Qualitative metrics (customer satisfaction):
   - Customer engineers can reproduce a deployment from the playbook in <= 2 hours during the workshop.
   - No more than two critical functional defects reported in acceptance testing.
   - Red-team sanity checks: hallucination rate on the eval prompts <= 6% (measured by manual label set of 200 prompts).

Workshop agenda (90 minutes, remote):
- 00–05 min: Introductions + goal alignment (Samira)
- 05–20 min: Proposed runtime architecture + cost/latency expectations (Ethan)
- 20–40 min: Live deploy walkthrough (infrastructure + k8s pod/profile flags)
- 40–60 min: Integration demo — prompt orchestration + caching hooks
- 60–80 min: Customer hands-on: run a validation prompt set with guidance (Priya)
- 80–90 min: Next steps, acceptance checklist, and signoff criteria (Samira + Diego)

Technical assumptions (call out early):
- Customer will provide a sampled dataset for eval that contains at least 200 domain-specific prompts and 200 ground-truth labels for quality checks.
- Network egress < 100 ms to Redwood Dedicated region us-west-2 for customer test VMs.
- Model variant: open-weight Llama-3x-small-quant (example), we will test both 4-bit and 8-bit quant variants.
- Customer agrees to share anonymized logs for the duration of the POC.

Pre-work (what we need from customer before workshop):
- Access: short-lived IAM role or SSH jump with instructions (ticket: JIRA-POC-419).
- Data: zipped eval prompts + expected outputs (s3://customer-samples/poc-eval.zip).
- Contact: two engineer contacts who can join the workshop and help run acceptance tests.

Deployment checklist (step-by-step, operator-facing):
- [ ] Reserve Dedicated pool: create reservation rsv-poc-DF-01 with 2xA10s (or equivalent)
- [ ] Provision demo VPC + security group rules (allow inbound from customer workshop IPs)
- [ ] Deploy model artifact to model catalog (tag: poc-df-2025-02)
- [ ] Configure policy: batching alpha-1, kv_cache enabled, prefix_cache thresholds at 512 tokens
- [ ] Enable telemetry hooks and retention 7d (for POC only)
- [ ] Run baseline synthetic test: 1000 requests at qps=15, collect p50/p95/p99
- [ ] Run customer eval set (200 prompts) and collect quality labels
- [ ] Snapshot configs and export runbook to GitHub repo linked above

Runbook triggers and immediate mitigations:
- Trigger: p95 latency > 600 ms for 10 consecutive minutes. Action: scale Dedicated pool by +1 GPU and reduce batch window by 20 ms. Page @infra-oncall.
- Trigger: error rate > 2% sustained. Action: rollback to previously known-good model variant and enable fallback route to hosted-lite.
- Trigger: hallucination rate spike > 10% on manual checks. Action: freeze rollout and run focused eval with prompt-guarding heuristics.

Risk register (top 5):
1) Data privacy: customer logs contain PHI. Mitigation: anonymize with redaction script (priorscript/redact-v1) and use short-lived tokens.
2) Network instability: if customer test VMs are on flaky VPN, latency targets can't be met. Mitigation: synthetic baseline from our test runner inside customer region.
3) Model regressions: open model update mid-POC. Mitigation: pin model sha and disallow auto-update.
4) Cost overrun: runaway token generation in misconfigured prompt. Mitigation: set per-session token cap at 1024 and circuit-breaker alerts.
5) Engineering bandwidth: customer team unavailable for scheduled workshop. Mitigation: have recorded deploy walkthrough and a 1:1 backup slot next week.

Acceptance signoff checklist (to be signed by customer PM & SE lead):
- Objective metrics documented and reproduced on a 48-hour window
- Runbook and configs committed to customer repo (or Redacted copy)
- Known issues list and mitigations logged
- Workshop completed and customer confirms they can reproduce deployment

Deliverables at POC close:
- Runbook + infra templates (Terraform snippet)
- Eval report (latency, cost, quality) with raw CSVs
- Short playbook for moving to Dedicated reserved contract
- Roadmap tasks (if successful) for production hardening

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: Should we recommend 8-bit over 4-bit by default for customer because of domain-specific token distribution? (Priya to run small head-to-head before workshop)
- Q: Confirm SLA wording we’ll offer in the POC report — Diego to coordinate with legal.
- TODO: create minimal terraform skeleton for Dedicated reservation and attach to PR. (Ethan)
- TODO: prepare a small set of guardrail prompt templates to reduce hallucination during eval. (Priya)

Helpful refs / links:
- Link to small deploy template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-kits/tree/main/dedicated-template
- Slack channel: #poc-inference-factory (invite Anika + her engineers)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ENG-8572 — evaluation rubric canonical page

Post-POC next-step recommendations (if successful):
- 30-day ramp plan: staged traffic shift 10/30/60 -> increased reserved capacity and canary monitoring
- Cost optimization: enable longer-lived prefix caching and recommend model quant tuning for production
- Security: if PHI present, propose Redwood Private with KMS integration and 90-day audit run

Notes (scratch):
- Keep the demo prompts domain-light for the workshop to reduce labeling friction.
- Consider running a short A/B with a smaller context window to measure token cost impact.
